blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Employee engagement has become a crowded concept — one that means different things to different stakeholders. For many executives, it is a quarterly number to be improved. For many employees, it is a survey they are weary of completing. Through sheer overuse, the concept has lost most of its analytical power.

A more useful frame is organisational health — the set of conditions that enable people to contribute sustainably: clarity of purpose, trust in leadership, quality of relationships, space for voice and dissent, and a sense of genuine progress. These conditions are harder to measure, but they correlate far more convincingly with long-term performance than any single engagement score.

The most important predictor of all is, perhaps surprisingly, the quality of the immediate manager. Years of data consistently show that people leave managers more often than they leave companies, and that a strong manager can protect engagement even in a turbulent environment. No amount of corporate initiative compensates for a weak local relationship.

items.q: According to the text, why has the concept of engagement lost most of its analytical power?
options: Because it has been overused and means different things to different people
Because surveys are too expensive to run
Because executives refuse to measure it
Because employees no longer understand the word
items.why: "a crowded concept… means different things to different stakeholders" e "Through sheer overuse, the concept has lost most of its analytical power".

items.q: How does the text describe the conditions that make up organisational health?
options: Easy to measure but weakly linked to performance
Harder to measure, yet more convincingly linked to long-term performance
Identical to a traditional engagement score
Relevant only in turbulent environments
items.why: "These conditions are harder to measure, but they correlate far more convincingly with long-term performance."

items.q: What is named as the single most important predictor of engagement?
options: The size of the corporate initiative budget
The frequency of employee surveys
The quality of the immediate manager
The seniority of the leadership team
items.why: "The most important predictor of all is… the quality of the immediate manager."

items.q: The text most strongly suggests that the author would DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A well-funded company-wide programme can offset a poor relationship with one's manager.
Trust in leadership belongs to organisational health.
A single engagement score is a limited measure.
Space for dissent is worth protecting.
items.why: Inferência: "No amount of corporate initiative compensates for a weak local relationship" contradiz diretamente essa ideia.

items.q: The line "a survey they are weary of completing" suggests that…
options: employees enjoy giving detailed feedback
employees have grown tired of being measured, likely without seeing change
surveys are too short to be useful
the surveys are anonymous
items.why: Inferência: "weary" indica fadiga — medir repetidamente sem ação gera cansaço, não engajamento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o novo índice à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. I want to be candid: the engagement score we report every quarter has quietly stopped mattering to this room. It moves a point or two, we nod, and nothing changes. That is not a measurement problem — it is a symptom of measurement without action.

So we are proposing to retire it. In its place, an organisational health index — five conditions we can actually influence: clarity of purpose, trust in leadership, quality of relationships, space for dissent, and a genuine sense of progress. Yes, these are harder to capture than a single number. But they track long-term performance far more faithfully, and, crucially, they tell us where to intervene.

One finding I want to flag before you see the deck. The strongest signal in the entire dataset is the quality of the immediate manager. People leave managers, not companies — and a strong manager protects a team even when everything around it is turbulent.

The uncomfortable implication is this: no glossy corporate initiative will rescue a team whose local relationship is broken. So I am asking us to shift the spend — away from the annual campaign, and towards developing the managers who actually hold this together.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Emily's central proposal to the leadership team?
options: To run the engagement survey more often
To retire the engagement score and replace it with an organisational health index
To outsource the measurement of engagement
To increase spending on the annual campaign
items.why: "we are proposing to retire it. In its place, an organisational health index."

items.q: How does Emily explain the fact that the engagement score "moves a point or two" and nothing changes?
options: It is a symptom of measurement without action
The survey sample is too small
The leadership team distrusts the vendor
The score is calculated incorrectly
items.why: "That is not a measurement problem — it is a symptom of measurement without action."

items.q: According to Emily, what is the strongest signal in the entire dataset?
options: The size of the annual campaign budget
The clarity of the company's mission statement
The quality of the immediate manager
The response rate to the survey
items.why: "The strongest signal in the entire dataset is the quality of the immediate manager."

items.q: What does Emily most likely want the leadership to do as a result of her findings?
options: Reallocate spending from the annual campaign towards developing managers
Cut the training budget entirely
Postpone any decision until next year
Keep the current score but rename it
items.why: Inferência: "I am asking us to shift the spend — away from the annual campaign, and towards developing the managers."

items.q: What does Emily imply by calling the finding an "uncomfortable implication"?
options: The data is unreliable and should be treated with caution
It challenges the value of the leadership's flagship corporate programmes
The managers were unwilling to be assessed
The health index will be too expensive to build
items.why: Inferência: é desconfortável porque implica que as iniciativas corporativas queridas da liderança não resolvem uma relação local quebrada.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need a systemic frame, not another isolated metric." A systemic frame means…
options: a way of seeing the whole set of interacting conditions
a single number on a dashboard
a rigid reporting structure
a short-term action plan
items.why: Systemic frame = visão sistêmica: enxergar o conjunto de condições que interagem, não uma métrica isolada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Teams that suppress every objection lose the ___ that keeps decisions honest."
options: dissent
hierarchy
headcount
compliance
items.why: Dissent = divergência: espaço para discordar mantém as decisões honestas.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "After the fourth pulse survey this year, staff reported clear ___ and stopped responding."
options: clarity of purpose
survey fatigue
belonging
organisational health
items.why: Survey fatigue = fadiga de pesquisa: cansaço de ser medido repetidamente sem ação.

items.q: Belonging is best described as…
options: the sense of being accepted and valued as part of a group
the ownership of company shares
the legal right to a job title
the length of service in a firm
items.why: Belonging = sentimento de pertencimento; não se reduz a um número no painel.

items.q: "A strong manager can hold a team together in a turbulent environment." This describes conditions that are…
options: calm and highly predictable
unstable, uncertain and fast-changing
strictly regulated
financially generous
items.why: Turbulent environment = ambiente turbulento: instável, incerto, em rápida mudança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se discute engajamento e saúde organizacional. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new health index." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
quietly ignore
criticise in public
postpone indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the manager-development programme across all sites next quarter." To roll out means to…
options: cancel in phases
implement in stages
test in secret
audit retroactively
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Several directors pushed back on retiring the old score." They…
options: approved it at once
resisted or challenged the idea
forgot about it
rewrote the whole index
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "HR launched the survey but never followed through on the results." They…
options: acted on every finding promptly
failed to carry the commitment to completion
delegated it to the board
published the raw data
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado — exatamente o que faltou.

items.q: "Another glossy campaign won't move the needle on belonging." This means it will…
options: make no noticeable difference
cost less than expected
provoke immediate resistance
take years to design
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
